/**
 * Exo covariance driver: mirrors PolyBench/C covariance.c but calls the Exo-generated kernel.
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "covariance.h"

/* Include the Exo-generated kernel header. */
#include "generated/covariance/covariance.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
                 DATA_TYPE *float_n,
                 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *float_n = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < M; j++)
      data[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*j) / M;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m,
                 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(cov,M,M,m,m))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("cov");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++) {
      if ((i * m + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, cov[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("cov");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}

/* Kernel implementation in Exo:

   The Exo code below defines a mathematically clear reference kernel
   and then applies a sequence of scheduling transformations to improve
   locality and parallelism:

   - Reorder the mean computation to traverse data row-major:
       for j: for i:  ->  for i: for j:
   - Tile and parallelize the data-centering loop over rows.
   - Restructure the covariance computation:
       * split initialization, accumulation, normalization, and
         symmetric copy into separate loops,
       * reorder j/k in the accumulation so we iterate over full rows,
       * tile the k-loop (rows) to improve cache reuse,
       * parallelize over the outer covariance row index i.
*/

/*
EXO START
from __future__ import annotations

from exo import *
from exo.API_scheduling import *
from exo.libs.memories import DRAM


# Reference implementation: mirrors the original PolyBench covariance kernel.
@proc
def kernel_covariance_base(
    m: size,
    n: size,
    float_n: DATA_TYPE,
    data: DATA_TYPE[n, m] @ DRAM,
    cov: DATA_TYPE[m, m] @ DRAM,
    mean: DATA_TYPE[m] @ DRAM,
):
    # Compute the mean of each column j over all rows i
    for j in seq(0, m):
        mean[j] = 0.0
        for i in seq(0, n):
            mean[j] += data[i, j]
        mean[j] = mean[j] / float_n

    # Center the data by subtracting the mean from each column
    for i in seq(0, n):
        for j in seq(0, m):
            data[i, j] = data[i, j] - mean[j]

    # Compute the covariance matrix (only upper triangle, then mirror)
    for i in seq(0, m):
        for j in seq(i, m):
            cov[i, j] = 0.0
            for k in seq(0, n):
                cov[i, j] += data[k, i] * data[k, j]
            cov[i, j] = cov[i, j] / (float_n - 1.0)
            cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]


# Tunable block sizes for cache optimization.
# These can be retuned for a particular machine without changing the C driver.
TI = 32  # tile size in the centering loop over the row dimension (n)
TK = 32  # tile size in the covariance accumulation over the row dimension (n)


# Start scheduling from the reference kernel.
kc = kernel_covariance_base


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Improve locality of the mean computation.
#
# Original structure:
#   for j in 0..m-1:
#       mean[j] = 0
#       for i in 0..n-1:
#           mean[j] += data[i, j]   # stride-n access in data
#       mean[j] /= float_n
#
# Target structure:
#   for j in 0..m-1: mean[j] = 0
#   for i in 0..n-1:
#       for j in 0..m-1:
#           mean[j] += data[i, j]   # row-major traversal of data
#   for j in 0..m-1: mean[j] /= float_n
#
# This keeps all arithmetic identical but walks `data` row-major.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Split the j-loop: [init | accumulation + normalization].
j0 = kc.find_loop("j")            # first j-loop (mean computation)
j0_body = j0.body()
kc = fission(kc, j0_body[0].after())

# Now the first j-loop only initializes mean[j],
# the second j-loop still does accumulation + normalization.
j1 = kc.find_loop("j #1")         # second j-loop (accum + normalize)
j1_body = j1.body()
kc = fission(kc, j1_body[0].after())

# We now have:
#   for j: mean[j] = 0
#   for j: for i: mean[j] += data[i,j]
#   for j: mean[j] /= float_n
#
# Reorder the accumulation loops so data is traversed row-major.
j_acc = kc.find_loop("j #1")      # j-loop that still wraps the i-loop
kc = reorder_loops(kc, j_acc)     # -> for i: for j: mean[j] += data[i,j]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Tile and parallelize the data-centering loop.
#
# Original:
#   for i in 0..n-1:
#       for j in 0..m-1:
#           data[i, j] -= mean[j]
#
# We tile i into (io, ii) to create coarse-grain parallel tiles, then
# parallelize the outer tile loop `io`. Each (io, ii) tile touches a
# disjoint set of rows, so this is race-free.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

i_center = kc.find_loop("i #1")   # second i-loop: the centering loop
kc = divide_loop(kc, i_center, TI, ("io", "ii"), tail="guard")

# Parallelize over tiles of rows.
io_center = kc.find_loop("io")
kc = parallelize_loop(kc, io_center)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Restructure the covariance computation.
#
# Original (inside the covariance section):
#   for i in 0..m-1:
#       for j in i..m-1:
#           cov[i,j] = 0
#           for k in 0..n-1:
#               cov[i,j] += data[k,i] * data[k,j]
#           cov[i,j] /= (float_n - 1)
#           cov[j,i] = cov[i,j]
#
# We perform the following steps:
#   - Split the j-loop body into four j-loops:
#       (a) initialize cov[i,j] = 0
#       (b) accumulate cov[i,j] over k
#       (c) normalize cov[i,j]
#       (d) write the symmetric element cov[j,i]
#   - Within (b), reorder j and k so that we iterate over full rows `k` and
#     then walk `j` row-major along `data[k, j]`.
#   - Tile the k-loop by TK to improve cache reuse on `data`.
#   - Parallelize the outer i-loop so each thread processes a distinct row
#     (and corresponding column in the symmetric write), avoiding races.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Outer i-loop of the covariance section (third i-loop in the procedure).
i_cov = kc.find_loop("i #2")

# Its body currently consists of a single j-loop that does:
#   (init, accumulate, normalize, copy).
j_all = i_cov.body()[0]
j_body = j_all.body()

# Split into:
#   j_init:  cov[i,j] = 0
#   j_rest:  [accumulate, normalize, copy]
kc = fission(kc, j_body[0].after())

# Re-acquire i-loop and the j-loop that still contains [accumulate, normalize, copy].
i_cov = kc.find_loop("i #2")
j_acc_norm_copy = i_cov.body()[1]
j_body = j_acc_norm_copy.body()

# Split into:
#   j_acc:   accumulation over k
#   j_rest:  [normalize, copy]
kc = fission(kc, j_body[0].after())

# Re-acquire i-loop and the j-loop that still contains [normalize, copy].
i_cov = kc.find_loop("i #2")
j_norm_copy = i_cov.body()[2]
j_body = j_norm_copy.body()

# Split into:
#   j_norm:  normalization
#   j_copy:  symmetric copy
kc = fission(kc, j_body[0].after())

# After these three fissions, inside each i-iteration we have:
#   j_init, j_acc, j_norm, j_copy  (all over j in [i, m)).

i_cov = kc.find_loop("i #2")
i_body = i_cov.body()
j_acc = i_body[1]                  # accumulation j-loop (second in the i-body)

# Reorder `j` and `k` in the accumulation so we iterate over full rows k:
#   before: for j in i..m-1: for k in 0..n-1: ...
#   after:  for k in 0..n-1: for j in i..m-1: ...
kc = reorder_loops(kc, j_acc)

# Tile the k-loop by TK inside the accumulation nest to improve cache reuse.
i_cov = kc.find_loop("i #2")
i_body = i_cov.body()
k_acc = i_body[1]                  # after reordering, the second stmt is the k-loop
kc = divide_loop(kc, k_acc, TK, ("ko", "ki"), tail="guard")

# Parallelize the outer covariance i-loop.
# Each i-iteration writes a disjoint set of (i,j) and (j,i) entries.
i_cov = kc.find_loop("i #2")
kc = parallelize_loop(kc, i_cov)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Export the scheduled kernel under the original external name.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

kernel_covariance = rename(kc, "kernel_covariance")

EXO END
*/


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE float_n;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(data,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(cov,DATA_TYPE,M,M,m,m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(mean,DATA_TYPE,M,m);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, &float_n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run Exo kernel. Flatten 2D views to 1D pointers. */
  kernel_covariance (/*ctxt=*/NULL, m, n,
                     (DATA_TYPE*)&float_n,
                     (DATA_TYPE*)POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data),
                     (DATA_TYPE*)POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov),
                     (DATA_TYPE*)POLYBENCH_ARRAY(mean));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(data);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(cov);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(mean);

  return 0;
}
